entries.title: Draft: Gaussian displacement model does not supply positional disorder
entries.statement: Unreviewed special-case derivation, awaiting w542. Let u be a real centered Gaussian vector field modulo constants with stationary increments in R^2 and spectral covariance Q(k)=aT|k|^-2 PT(k)+aL|k|^-s PL(k) on 0<|k|<=Lambda, with measure d^2k/(2pi)^2, Lambda>0, aT>0, aL>=0 and 0<=s<2; PL=kk^t/|k|^2, PT=I-PL. For fixed q!=0 and unit e, E exp(i q.(u(r e)-u(0))) is bounded above and below by positive multiples of r^-eta at large r, eta=aT|q|^2/(4pi). For theta=curl(u)/2, the uncentered sixfold correlation tends to exp(-36aT Lambda^2/(16pi))>0. The centered correlation instead tends to zero. These are surrogate observables; their identification with a Riesz particle Gibbs law is unproved. A defect-free Gaussian displacement calculation does not establish the fast positional decay of a proposed hexatic regime.
assumptions: Explicit Gaussian spectral model, not an established microscopic Riesz limit
Fixed nonzero q and direction; finite ultraviolet cutoff

entries.title: Draft: Critical L2 error can erase a bounded correlation
entries.statement: Unreviewed finite counterexample, awaiting w542. For 0<h<1, let U,V in {-1,1} have joint law P(U=u,V=v)=(1+h u v)/4. Set A0=B0=U, Ar=V and Br=(V-hU)/(1+h). All are centered and bounded by one. Then E[A0 Ar]=h, E[B0 Br]=0, ||B0-A0||2=0 and ||Br-Ar||2^2=2h^2/(1+h). Thus an unspecified L2 error O(h) does not preserve a positive lower correlation bound of order h. For centered reference observables of L2 norm at most M and both observable errors at most delta, expansion and Cauchy-Schwarz give a correlation error at most 2M delta+delta^2. A sufficiently small explicit relative constant or o(h) can preserve the leading correlation; the example does not challenge such hypotheses. This is a finite transfer obstruction, not a constructed Riesz Gibbs state.
assumptions: General bounded observables; no geometric or Gibbs identification
New derivation requires w542 independent check

entries.title: P0321 draft: unresolved microscopic transfer obligation
entries.statement: Open proof obligation, not a theorem. In a proposed classical density-one 1/r jellium subtarget, choose a nonempty open inverse-temperature interval and construct actual equilibrium thermodynamic limits. A cumulant-based angular route must derive a real lifted angle difference with logarithmic variance and uniform absolutely summable higher cumulants at charge 6, and a microscopic bond representation C6,L(r)=A_L,r E exp(i6 X_L,r)+epsilon_L,r with |A_L,r| uniformly bounded above and away from zero and insertion error smaller than the leading algebraic correlation. The same state must separately lack crystalline positional quasi-long-range order. Defect-sector control, the angle lift, the amplitude and insertion estimates, and positional disorder remain unproved. For an iterated thermodynamic-then-distance limit, vanishing errors at each fixed distance can suffice under convergence of the specified observables; simultaneous limits need extra uniformity. The historical P0321 record and its source are qualitative; current openness remains UNKNOWN, and this selected quantitative route is not the exact full conjecture.
assumptions: Chosen s=1 classical jellium convention, not an all-exponent claim
The w540 conditional proof route was audited, not promoted to a full target proof
